headline: Short-term holders turn to loss-selling, STH-SOPR at 0.9916; ETFs bleed $430M in a day and dollar money stays away.
summary: After price broke their cost, short-term holders started selling at a loss and 1–2-year holders joined, but daily realized losses are only a third of the June low, so this is not capitulation. ETFs lost $430M on Nov 5, stablecoins shrank 2.6% in a week and the Coinbase premium is still negative: bids and leveraged longs are holding price, not new money. Watch the 75,000 bid wall, the estimated liquidation band below 73,800 and the 200-day MA at 73,191.

overview.lead: Price sat still just under the short-term holder cost, but behavior underneath changed: sellers moved from paper losses to realized losses, dollar money kept leaving, and the bid wall at 75,000 plus paying longs are what holds price.
points: Today's finding: STH-SOPR 1.0015 → 0.9916 (CheckOnChain Nov 6); short-term holders realized 4,299 BTC of losses, more than their profits; LTH-SOPR 0.9385 (Bitview).

Macro: October payrolls +165K vs 59K expected, December hike odds up to about 79%; the Nasdaq bounced 1.9% but BTC did not follow, closing at 75,742 (−0.31%).
Bull day 29; the 200-day MA at 73,191 is 3.4% below; no exit-framework trigger.

news.read: Strong jobs push hike odds higher, a headwind for BTC. findings.title: Short-term holders start selling at a loss, and 1–2-year holders join in
findings.lean_why: Selling has moved from paper losses to realized losses and spread to holders of one to two years; supply is thin from 74K to 66K, so price could move fast if 74K gives way.
findings.what: Question: after price broke the short-term holder cost, who is selling and who will absorb it below? Sellers have flipped from small gains to losses, and not only short-term traders: holders of one to two years are also selling at a loss. STH-SOPR 1.0015 → 0.9916, LTH-SOPR 0.9385 (CheckOnChain, Bitview, Nov 6).
findings.why: Breakdown: short-term holders realized 3,833 BTC of profit versus 4,299 of loss (ratio 0.89, 1.32 a week ago); versus 7 days ago profit −17.7%, loss +22.2%, so more loss-taking drove it (CheckOnChain Nov 6). By holding time, of 30-day realized losses, under 1 month is 49.7%, 1–2 years 35.8% (30.9% 30 days ago), 6–12 months 10.4% (Bitview). Cost map (CheckOnChain actual coin age, Nov 6): short-term holders 3.734M BTC at an average 75,214; thickest bands 76K (590K), 80K (580K), 62K (495K); 30 days earlier (Bitview actual, Oct 6) 3.563M at 74,173. Cross-check: network realized profit ÷ loss 0.486 on Nov 6, 7-day avg 0.817 (CheckOnChain); net realized P/L −$1.586B over 7 days versus −$230M the week before (CoinMetrics Nov 5). Contradiction: network realized loss $733M, 4.82 bp of market cap, versus 13.2 at the Jun 30 low and 47.2 on Feb 5 (Bitview), far from capitulation; illiquid supply +1.64% in 7 days (Nov 5, 100th percentile of the year), so someone is also locking coins away.
findings.alt: STH-SOPR is daily, lags about a day and is smoothed, so concentrated intraday loss-selling gets averaged out. Holders of 1–2 years mostly bought between Nov 2024 and Nov 2025, largely above today's price, so part of their rising loss share is just the passage of time. LTH-SOPR and realized loss are per-UTXO, not entity-adjusted, so exchange wallet consolidation is included; the 30-day turnover split (who sold) is an estimate, with modeled STH total 3.8% off the actual and 11.7% of coins in the wrong band.
findings.history: STH-SOPR dropped below 1 nine times in the past year; median 30-day move −0.6% (baseline +0.6%); the last five: −15.2%, −2.8%, +4.2%, +21.3%, −7.3%, no consistent direction. This dip (0.9916) is almost the same depth as Oct 30 (0.9918); the system tags it 'heavier' but the gap is tiny.
findings.so: Logic chain: yesterday seventy percent of short-term supply was only at a paper loss; today some of it is being realized, so the 'not yet capitulating' view in 2026-11-05-1 is starting to give (its 0.99 confirmation line is not hit yet). But the loss size is a third of the June low, so selling is just starting, not a completed flush. Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 6): at a 74,000 close, 2.605M short-term BTC would be underwater, about 70%; at 66,000 only 2.696M, jumping to 3.097M at 64,000. Below 74K there is no thick cost zone until the mid-60s. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 13: short-term holder realized loss above 5,000 BTC, meaning loss-taking is scaling up, confirms; a close back above 78,000 (back over the thickest supply) refutes.

findings.title: ETFs, stablecoins and the Coinbase premium: all three dollar channels draining
findings.lean_why: Dollars available to buy BTC are shrinking and the average ETF buyer is underwater, so rallies may meet break-even selling; bids and leverage, not new money, are holding price.
findings.what: Dollar money did not come back this week: ETFs lost $430M on Nov 5, stablecoins shrank 2.62% in a week, and the Coinbase premium 7-day average is still −0.157% (Farside, DefiLlama, our data, Nov 5–6).
findings.why: ETF breakdown: Nov 2–5 total −$870M with only Nov 4 positive; on Nov 5 FBTC −$199.9M, IBIT −$105M, with IBIT about −$1.04B over 5 straight sessions (Decrypt citing Farside). Estimated ETF holder cost 80,441 (ex-GBTC, Nov 4), close 4.2% below it. Stablecoins $293.7B, −$14.2B over 30 days (DefiLlama Nov 6). Cross-check: Coinbase premium −0.149% daily; OKX spot taker delta −2,094 BTC on Nov 6 (OKX only); Korea premium 7-day avg 0.64%, below its long-run median of 1.12%; Asian OTC USDT/CNY −0.42% (snapshot). Contradiction: weighted funding rose from 7.57% to 8.59%, so perp longs are being added, the opposite of spot. Macro: payrolls +165K, December hike odds about 79% (TokenPost); Nasdaq +1.9% while BTC did not follow.
findings.alt: Nov 5 ETF flow is provisional (Farside and SoSoValue agree) and will be overwritten when The Block publishes; ETF cost is estimated from daily flow ÷ close. Stablecoin supply spans all chains and issuers and may include redemptions after exchange-specific events we cannot separate. The Coinbase premium compares Coinbase with Binance only and misses CME and OTC.
findings.history: Prior 7-day stablecoin plunges (2% tail of the year): after 2026-01-28 the next 30 days were −26.1%, after 2026-06-06 +5.2%; n=2, too few, background only. Since Jan 2024, price has closed below the estimated ETF cost on 165 of 707 days, deepest −26.4% (2026-06-30).
findings.so: What changed is where ETF holders stand: their 80,441 average cost is now overhead break-even supply, overlapping the 580K BTC short-term band at 80K. What did not change is the source of support: still the $244M bid at 75,000 (Hyperliquid perps) and longs paying 8.59% funding, not fresh cash. Conditional: trading into 73,800–74,800 would trigger a batch of estimated long liquidations (estimate, OKX only). Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 13: stablecoins below $290B, meaning money keeps leaving, confirms; Coinbase premium 7-day average back above −0.05%, meaning US spot buyers return, refutes.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: BTC about −10% from the September high, retesting the August breakout; STH supply in profit fell from ≥97.5% to about 38%; true market mean 77.7K, STH cost basis 75.7K, 200-day MA inside the 73–76K band, long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K; after the past three midterms BTC fell another 15–50% within 2–10 weeks. Conclusion: holding 73–76K is a healthy reset within the August uptrend; a break below 73K points to a longer consolidation.
items.meaning: The Nov 6 close of 75,742 is in the middle of its 73–76K band, where our STH cost (75,887) and 200-day MA (73,191) also sit; its 'break below 73K' nearly coincides with our hedge line at 73,191. The midterm history is only 3 cases, so we do not use it for the call.
